doc.title: Victor Rendon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Rumba and the label salsa
summary: Rendón recalls being confused by the term rumba and sees salsa as a generic label.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: And the rumba, there was a label R – H – U – M – B - A that was confusing for me in my younger days because here I am learning rumba — R – U – M – B – A, the traditional folkloric way, then you have the rumbas of Xavier Cugat, you know and all that, from back in the 30s, 40s and 50s. And I kind of realized it was just a term, a label that they put on the music. And like where I come from it was mostly musica tropical, you know, tropical music. And later on in the 60s the term salsa came into the scene and now it’s called salsa. So it’s like a blanket generic term for the music. But it’s not necessarily a rhythm you know.
